summary: 施釉炻器，带化妆土彩绘装饰，吉州窑
description: 江西省中部的吉州窑窑口为与中国其他窑口竞争而生产深色瓷器，因此吉州窑陶工极具创造力。他们的部分作品是在器物上施一层白色化妆土，并在其上绘制具有强烈视觉效果的醒目图案。这种引人注目的水波纹设计令人称奇，画师将瓶的整个表面转化为动态翻滚的水体，并以翻腾的浪花加以凸显。吉州窑瓷器在长江三角洲下游城市（包括南京、上海、常州、泰州）以及安徽省、韩国和日本均有出土。吉州窑烧制时，化妆土涂层和镶嵌装饰会呈现柔和的象牙色，而暴露的胎体则呈现温暖的桂皮色。

originalMetadata.title: Vase (Meiping) with Waves
culture: China, Jiangxi Province, Yonghezhen, Yuan dynasty (1271–1368)
originalMetadata.technique: glazed stoneware with slip painted decoration, Jizhou ware
originalMetadata.description: Jizhou ware kilns in central Jiangxi province produced a dark ware in competition with other kilns in China and so Jizhou potters were highly inventive. Part of their work is a ware covered with a white slip over which they painted bold graphic designs of great visual effect. This striking wave design is remarkable in the way the painter transformed the entire surface of the vase into dynamically rolling masses of water, highlighted by cresting waves. Jizhou wares were excavated in cities of the lower Yangzi delta, including Nanjing, Shanghai, Changzhou, Taizhou, as well as Anhui province, Korea, and Japan.
originalMetadata.did_you_know: When Jizhou ware is fired, the slip coating and the inlaid decoration assume a soft ivory color while the exposed clay body displays a warm cinnamon brown.

name: 青花双狮头罐
description: 此罐因其鲜明的造型轮廓、浓艳的青蓝色泽以及坚劲利落的纹饰线条而备受称赞，是元代青花瓷的经典范例。此类器物最迟在14世纪30年代便已生产，兼供国内（宫廷与民间）及海外贸易使用。该件器物见证了因贸易而在中国与大蒙古国其他地区之间展开的艺术观念与工艺技术的交流。用于釉下青花装饰的钴料进口自伊朗，可能出自卡尚。如此器所见，以缠枝花卉为底衬的云肩凤纹带，也是伊利汗国时期（1256–1353年）伊朗装饰艺术中常见的一种艺术语汇。该器肩部白釉上刻划有“宫”与“南”字样，表明其曾藏于宫廷内的特定场所。

originalMetadata.title: Jar with Lion-Head Handles
culture: China, Jiangxi Province, Jingdezhen, Yuan dynasty (1271–1368)
originalMetadata.technique: porcelain with underglaze painted decoration
originalMetadata.description: Appreciated for its strong profile, brilliant blue color, and firm delineation of the decorative patterns, this jar is a classic example of Yuan dynasty blue-and-white ware. This type of ware was produced no later than the 1330s for both domestic use (the court and common people alike) and overseas trade. This example testifies to the transmission of artistic ideas and techniques between China and the rest of the great Mongol Empire as a result of trade. The cobalt that was used for the blue underglaze decoration was imported from Iran, likely from Kashan. The band of cloud-collar motifs with phoenixes set against floral grounds, as shown here, is an artistic vocabulary that can also be found in Iranian decorative arts of the Ilkhanid period (1256–1353).
originalMetadata.did_you_know: The characters for "palace" and "south" are scratched into the white glaze on the vessel's shoulder, suggesting that it was once kept in a specific location in a palace.

originalMetadata.title: Prunus Vase (Meiping) with Blossoming Lotus
culture: China, Jiangxi Province, Jingdezhen kilns, Ming dynasty (1368–1644)
originalMetadata.technique: Porcelain with polychrome glazes, Fahua ware
originalMetadata.description:
According to 11th-century poet Zhou Dunyi, “all people like peonies, but I alone like the lotus because it emerges from the mud unstained.” The lotus is a symbol of purity and popular among Chinese literati and in Buddhism. This vase shows lotus flowers rising from the water’s surface depicted in elegant yet simple ripples.

Made in a kiln at Jingdezhen in southern China, this vase is an example of the fahua technique—decoration with raised outlines produced by squeezing clay from a tube onto the vase’s surface. Colors are applied to fill the outlines before firing.

culture: China, Jiangxi province, Jingdezhen kilns, Ming dynasty (1368-1644)
originalMetadata.technique: Porcelain with sweet-white (tianbai; 甜白) glaze
originalMetadata.description: White was a ritual color used in Buddhist ceremonies, as well as the color of mourning. The jar may have been used as a planter, a vase for flowers, or it may have held incense sticks on a home altar.
